display.purpose: League Gothic 400, uppercase, line-height 0.92-0.95. Flyer headlines and the title card only; house-rules statements set on poster stock in the pride inks.

body.purpose: Atkinson Hyperlegible. Print-out copy and telemetry sheets; figures in tabular-nums. Base 1rem / line-height 1.5 = 24px on the 8px baseline.

typed.purpose: Courier Prime on index cards with line-height exactly 24px so copy sits on the printed ruling; also buttons, channel labels, stamps, and the footer.

hand.purpose: Shantell Sans 500 in the six pride inks. Annotations, captions, and the greeting only — never body copy; always slightly rotated (-2 to +1.5 deg).

shadows.name: pin-shadow
shadows.purpose: The one shadow of the world: every paper artifact at rest, hung on the cork.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: Hover/focus-within on interactive paper, paired with translate: 0 1px — the note presses toward the cork; shadows shrink, never grow.

shadows.name: brass-cast
shadows.purpose: The brass pin's own tight cast — hardware only.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The single micro-motion gesture: hover settles a pinned artifact's tilt from 1.2x to 0.35x its step and presses interactive paper toward the cork. Gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: thread-draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 -> 0; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range tuned per segment (pathLength="1")
motion.purpose: The crimson thread draws itself as the wall scrolls. The CSS default state is fully drawn — animation only rewinds it — so reduced motion, engines without animation-timeline, and no-JS all land on the designed resolved state. Gated behind @supports (animation-timeline: view()).

motion.name: spine-grow
motion.value: scale 1 0 -> 1 1, transform-origin top; animation-timeline: view(); cover 0% -> 30-40%
motion.purpose: The straight spine segments (timeline, mid-page wall run) grow downward ahead of the reading edge.

motion.name: stitch-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) -> inset(-8px); animation-timeline: view(); cover 14% -> 24%
motion.purpose: Stretched connector SVGs reveal by clip wipe instead of dash draw: Chromium does not pathLength-normalize dasharray under vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke, so dash-drawn threads are only safe at 1:1 scale.

narrative.overview:
The site is a career pinned to a cork wall by its owner's hand. One crimson thread — *der rote Faden*, German for both a literal red thread and a story's through-line — enters at a stamped 12/2019 pin in the hero, stitches every artifact in chronological order down the whole page, and is cut in a loose knot on open cork just before the contact corner. Everything on screen is a physical object on that wall: typed index cards, flyer posters, clean print-outs, polaroids, handwritten margin notes, brass pins, circular rubber stamps. The world refuses the dark-neon developer-dashboard default and the neutral CV alike (the direction contract committed in `src/layouts/main.astro`).

The wall proves instead of asserting. Every figure on it carries its unit and its as-of date; standalone dates arrive as hand-pressed stamps; telemetry hangs as annotated chart print-outs with the data repeated in a folded table. The six pride inks are the owner's working colors — they write the margin notes and encode the chart series — and the house-rules flyer states in League Gothic that removing them makes the wall stop making sense. Two durable brand commitments live here: the handwritten Lottie greeting (drawn in pride inks) survives every redesign, and queer-friendliness is expressed openly as identity, not decoration.

Density is a curated collage: artifacts cluster, overlap, and tilt, but a hidden 12-column grid organizes every placement and the tilt comes in fixed ±1.2° steps. Motion is quiet and physical — the thread draws itself as the wall scrolls, pins settle in 150ms, and every animation has a designed resolved state that stands on its own wherever motion is unwelcome or unsupported.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, light, paper-on-cork material world (`color-scheme: light` only; no dark theme).
One structural accent — the crimson thread — plus six rationed pride inks doing real work (annotation + data series), never decoration.
Four typefaces, one per physical material; faces never mix inside a single artifact.
Hidden 12-column grid under a tilted collage; rotation in ±1.2° steps, neighbors never share a tilt.
One shadow, one grain texture; depth is physical stacking (thread behind paper, pins above it), never glow.
Scroll-drawn thread and 150ms settle micro-motion, each with a fully-drawn/resolved fallback state.
Every figure set with unit + as-of date; stamps date the wall itself.

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: `--thread` is the only structural accent. It may be thread, stamp ink, focus ring, underline, or headline rule — never a large fill, and never joined by a second red.

rules.name: The Working Ink Rule
rules.body: The six pride inks are load-bearing: they annotate the wall and encode the data series, and the house-rules flyer says so in type ("remove them and the wall stops making sense"). An ink that is neither writing a note nor naming a series has no business on the wall.

rules.name: The Paper Slip Rule
rules.body: Handwritten ink goes on paper, not raw cork. Every pride ink clears 4.5:1 on `--paper`; green, violet, and blue do not clear raw cork, so freestanding notes ride small paper slips with the pin shadow.

rules.name: The One Material Rule
rules.body: Every artifact is one physical material. A flyer is League Gothic only, an index card Courier Prime only, a print-out Atkinson Hyperlegible only, an annotation Shantell Sans only. Faces never mix inside one artifact — the greeting card is all hand material, including its Lottie.

rules.name: The Ruled Card Rule
rules.body: Typed index cards print their own ruling — a red header rule at 40px and blue lines every 24px — and the typed face's 24px line-height sits the copy exactly on those lines. Break the rhythm and the card reads as a forgery.

rules.name: The Unit-and-Date Rule
rules.body: Every figure is set with its unit and its as-of date ("2.4M+ users on 8,357 servers, as of 2026-08-03"; "3,019.9 h"). Standalone dates are stamped, with "as of" as the stamp's sub-line. A bare number is not a fact on this wall.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every artifact hangs on the same pin shadow. Interaction presses paper toward the cork — shadows shrink on hover, they never grow, and nothing glows.

rules.name: The Behind-the-Paper Rule
rules.body: The thread runs behind the paper and never crosses printed text. It surfaces only where cork shows; where an artifact must sit over it (the flagship IHK card), the thread demonstratively dips beneath and re-emerges.

rules.name: The Resolved State Rule
rules.body: Every animation is a progressive enhancement over a designed resolved state — the thread fully drawn, the greeting hand-set, tilts already applied. Reduced motion, missing `animation-timeline` support, or failed JS must land on a state that was designed, not degraded.

rules.name: The 150ms Settle Rule
rules.body: Micro-motion is one gesture: 150ms ease-out. Hover settles a pinned artifact's tilt toward 0.35× and presses it toward the cork. Nothing bounces, springs, or runs longer than 150ms except the scroll-driven thread.

rules.name: The Taut Thread Rule
rules.body: The thread is under tension: dead-straight runs pin to pin, and brass pins appear only on cards (owner decisions, 2026-08-04). The timeline has no spine — each row runs one straight connector from its card pin to the next card pin (stretched corner-to-corner SVG, dasharray disabled for Chromium). Hero paths come from src/components/wall/taut.ts with a ~7px wrap at each pin. Section-seam corners tuck behind paper; the only slack is the cut end's knot.

dos: Do pin every new artifact properly: paper or aged-paper ground, the single pin shadow, a brass pin bridging the top edge, and a tilt step from {−1, 0, 1} — neighbors never share a tilt.
Do set every figure with its unit and as-of date, and stamp standalone dates ("as of" sub + ISO date). A number without provenance doesn't go on the wall.
Do keep handwritten pride ink on paper — put freestanding notes on paper slips; green, violet, and blue do not clear 4.5:1 on raw cork.
Do design the resolved state first and gate motion behind `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; the CSS default state is the finished one.
Do draw new icons in the house grammar: 24px viewBox, stroke 1.75, `currentColor`, round caps and joins, a deliberate waver in every path.
Do keep the wall's German artifacts German with `lang="de"` — "Werdegang", "2010 – heute", the HEUTE stamp — the market literacy is part of the design.
donts: Don't use glass, blur, glow, gradient text, or dark surfaces — the world explicitly refused the dark-neon dashboard; the only gradients alive are the brass sphere and the printed card rulings.
Don't add kickers or eyebrow labels above headings. A flyer carries its headline, a hand-drawn thread rule, and at most one dateline.
Don't mix faces inside one artifact — no Courier on a flyer, no League Gothic on an index card, no hand face as body copy.
Don't put facts on the house-rules flyer: it carries values only; every measured claim lives on the quiet typed record card beside it.
Don't move the free-forever promise off Ayako's cluster — it is Ayako's own flyer, quoted, with the license line on the v3 card, never a site-wide banner.
Don't let the AI-workflow story outscale the human record: it stays a subordinate typed index card; the values flyer stays the louder artifact.
Don't let the thread cross printed text or sit above paper — it runs behind and surfaces in cork gaps only.
Don't introduce a second red or spend `--thread` on fills; it is thread, stamp ink, focus ring, and underline — its scarcity is the structure.
